angle_title: The core lessons of Atomic Habits, distilled for a first-time reader
angle_summary: James Clear's Atomic Habits is the definitive modern book on behavior change. Its most shareable ideas — systems over goals, 1% better, identity-based habits, making good habits obvious/easy — translate cleanly into a book-summary post that drives saves.

supporting_facts.fact: Atomic Habits argues that improving 1% every day compounds to roughly 37 times better over a year, and that people fall to the level of their systems rather than rising to their goals.

voice_compatibility_notes: Use 5 lessons for a first-timer. Keep each lesson punchy and concrete; reference the book directly. No fabricated quotes.

angle_title: Inversion: solving problems backward the way Charlie Munger does
angle_summary: Inversion — asking how to fail and then avoiding it — is one of the most practical mental models. Munger credits much of his success to avoiding stupidity rather than seeking brilliance. Great as a list or mini-blog.

supporting_facts.fact: Charlie Munger popularized inversion with the line 'All I want to know is where I'm going to die, so I'll never go there,' framing problem-solving as avoiding failure modes.

voice_compatibility_notes: Concrete everyday examples of inverting a problem. Attribute the model to Munger. No investment advice.
